column1: # products.tsv -- controlled vocabulary of fermentation products tracked by fermdb.
# One row per product. `tier` is a stored property that drives acquisition policy in code
# (PLAN.md B.1) -- it is read by code, never re-implemented as an `if product == ...` branch
# (docs/reference/CONVENTIONS.md, "Code"). Tiers, per PLAN.md B.1:
#   primary   -- isobutanol. Comprehensive across all hosts and data types.
#   reference -- ethanol. Bounded, capped, admitted only against a stated B.3 criterion.
#   adjacent  -- captured only when measured alongside isobutanol in the same experiment
#               (co-reported Ehrlich-pathway higher alcohols; PLAN.md B.1).
#   reserved  -- rows with no data yet. They exist to prove the schema is product-generic
#               (PLAN.md section U) and must never be silently populated from a guess.
# D5: theoretical mass/molar yields moved OUT of this file and into
# data/vocabularies/theoretical_yields.tsv, keyed by (product_id, substrate). Glucose was
# previously an unnamed assumption baked into this file's column names
# (`glucose_mw_g_mol`, and implicitly every `theoretical_yield_*` column); it is now a named
# `substrate` value in theoretical_yields.tsv instead, so a future non-glucose substrate is a new
# row there, not a schema change here.
# Columns:
#   tier                        primary | reference | adjacent | reserved
#   id                          internal CURIE, YAA:PRODUCT:<slug> (docs/reference/CONVENTIONS.md
#                               "Identifiers") -- this is the join key theoretical_yields.tsv uses
#   name                        common name used elsewhere in the atlas
#   chebi_id                    external identifier, Bioregistry `chebi:` prefix form
#   formula                     molecular formula (neutral species used for mass-yield purposes;
#                               see evidence when the row's chebi_id is the conjugate acid/base
#                               of what "product" commonly names)
#   carbon_number               carbon atoms per formula
#   canonical_unit              the unit this atlas reports the product's titer/production in
#   product_mw_g_mol            molar mass of this product (an intrinsic property of the product,
#                               unlike a yield, which is a property of a (product, substrate) pair
#                               and so now lives in theoretical_yields.tsv)
# Every row carries 'evidence' (free text naming the source) and 'confidence'
# (docs/reference/CONVENTIONS.md, "Curation"). The confidence vocabulary is closed and has four
# values everywhere ('unverified', 'low', 'medium', 'high'; D2). Confidence is never 'high' from
# memory alone, and never 'high' when the evidence is only another fermdb file (PLAN.md, another
# vocabulary TSV, or a source module) rather than something checked outside the repo -- that is
# citing memory with an extra hop (see compartments.tsv). Where a chebi id/formula/molar mass was
# actually looked up against ChEBI in this session, that check is named and confidence is 'high';
# everything else recalled from PLAN.md or general chemistry knowledge is capped at 'medium' or
# marked 'unverified'.
